biological-foundation-model.name: Biological foundation model (FM)
biological-foundation-model.def: A model trained on millions of DNA, protein, or single-cell measurements, whose general patterns are extracted once and then reused for many downstream problems. The term "foundation model" (2021) describes models trained on broad data and adaptable to a wide range of tasks.

agentic-system.name: Agentic system
agentic-system.def: An AI assistant built on a large language model that runs multistep analyses from plain-language requests and increasingly calls FMs as tools. It is not a model itself: it coordinates an LLM, the user, and many tools.

knowledge-boundary.name: Knowledge boundary
knowledge-boundary.def: The range of inputs, tasks, and conditions over which a model's outputs can be relied upon.

knowledge-extraction.name: Knowledge extraction from data
knowledge-extraction.def: The goal that has driven each stage of computation in biology: getting from raw data to signal, to interpretation, and now to discovery.

embedding.name: Embedding
embedding.def: A long list of numbers (hundreds to thousands) that a model assigns to each token of an input, capturing the token's intrinsic properties and its context. Embeddings cannot be read directly, but because all embeddings from one model share a numeric space, inputs with similar properties lie close together. They serve as the reusable intermediate form of raw data (a protein sequence becomes a sequence embedding).

compression-vs-composability.name: Compression vs. composability
compression-vs-composability.def: Two ways of building a tool that extracts knowledge: FMs compress data into one learned representation, whereas agents compose separate existing tools into a workflow.

correlation-vs-causation.name: Correlation vs. causation
correlation-vs-causation.def: Two ways of extracting knowledge from data: FMs learn patterns of what occurs together (correlation), and can predict accurately without having learned the mechanism that drives the phenomenon (causation).

llm.name: Large language model (LLM)
llm.def: The language model an agent uses as its source of reasoning to plan tasks. Its knowledge is restricted to what has previously been documented.

self-supervised-learning.name: Self-supervised learning
self-supervised-learning.def: A way of training in which part of each training example is hidden ("masked") and the model predicts it from the parts that remain visible, so the training targets come from the raw data itself and no human labels are needed.

supervised-learning.name: Supervised learning
supervised-learning.def: Training in which humans annotate ("supervise") the data.

probing.name: Probing
probing.def: Passing a model's embedding of each input to a separate, much simpler model (e.g., a linear regression) that is trained on a small labeled dataset to predict a property of interest.

fine-tuning.name: Fine-tuning
fine-tuning.def: Training the FM itself further on a small labeled dataset.

zero-shot-prediction.name: Zero-shot prediction
zero-shot-prediction.def: Using a model with no labeled data at all, for example scoring how plausible a sequence is and using that score as an estimate of variant effect.

vocabulary.name: Vocabulary
vocabulary.def: The set of basic units a model can recognize, analogous to the words of a language.

token.name: Token
token.def: One vocabulary unit as it occurs in a particular input, so that an input is read as a sequence of tokens, much as a sentence is read as a sequence of words.

grammar.name: Grammar
grammar.def: The set of rules by which a model's units are combined. In biology these rules are largely unknown, unlike human language.

regulatory-dna.name: Regulatory DNA
regulatory-dna.def: Noncoding sequences, such as promoters and enhancers, that control when, where, and how strongly a gene is transcribed.

tf-binding-motif.name: Transcription factor (TF) binding motif
tf-binding-motif.def: A short sequence, typically 6 to 12 base pairs long, that is preferentially bound by a particular TF.

corpus.name: Corpus
corpus.def: The large repository of data on which a model is trained (plural: corpora).

sparse-autoencoder.name: Sparse autoencoder
sparse-autoencoder.def: An auxiliary model that re-expresses each embedding as a combination of a much larger set of features, each of which tends to correspond to a single property.

five-design-elements.name: The five design elements
five-design-elements.def: The five parts that together describe nearly any biological FM, and each of which sets part of its knowledge boundary: data (training corpus and tokenization), model architecture (how information is processed and stored), training scheme (what the model is rewarded to learn), evaluation scheme (how the model is judged), and post-analysis (how a trained model is used).

generalization.name: Generalization
generalization.def: Making useful predictions for inputs the model did not encounter during training.

transformer.name: Transformer and self-attention
transformer.def: The leading architecture, whose self-attention relates every token to every other token in the input. It lets distant positions interact, at a cost that grows roughly quadratically with input length.

inductive-bias.name: Inductive bias
inductive-bias.def: Built-in, modality-specific assumptions of an architecture. Transformers have few, which lets them adapt to very different corpora but generally requires larger training sets.

masked-language-modeling.name: Masked language modeling
masked-language-modeling.def: A training approach in which randomly hidden tokens are predicted from the surrounding sequence.

autoregressive-modeling.name: Autoregressive modeling
autoregressive-modeling.def: A training approach in which each token is predicted from those before it, which makes these models natural generators of new sequences.

contrastive-learning.name: Contrastive / metric learning
contrastive-learning.def: A training approach that pulls related examples close together in embedding space and pushes unrelated ones apart.

intrinsic-vs-downstream-evaluation.name: Intrinsic vs. downstream evaluation
intrinsic-vs-downstream-evaluation.def: Two levels of evaluating a model. Intrinsic evaluation asks whether the model has learned the structure of its data; downstream evaluation asks whether it helps with a practical task, increasingly on shared benchmarks. The two do not always agree.

transfer-learning.name: Transfer learning
transfer-learning.def: Carrying knowledge captured in the embedding during pretraining over to a new task by probing or fine-tuning, so that a small labeled dataset suffices where training from scratch would require a large one.

in-silico-perturbation.name: In silico perturbation
in-silico-perturbation.def: Simulating a change, such as deleting a gene, and observing how a cell's embedding shifts.

interpretability-analysis.name: Interpretability analysis
interpretability-analysis.def: Analysis of how a model arrives at its outputs, for example which input positions drive a prediction or which internal features match known biology. It can reveal whether a model relies on genuine biology or on shortcuts in the data.

inputs-vs-outputs.name: Inputs vs. outputs (data axis, task axis)
inputs-vs-outputs.def: Two axes for organizing biological FMs: inputs (the type of biological data) and outputs (the task the model performs). Inputs differ mainly in vocabulary, corpus, and architecture; outputs mainly in training scheme and post-analysis.

bulk-rna-seq.name: Bulk RNA sequencing
bulk-rna-seq.def: A measurement of the average expression of all cells in a tissue sample, which loses cellular resolution.

spatial-transcriptomics.name: Spatial transcriptomics
spatial-transcriptomics.def: A measurement that records where each cell sits in a tissue section.

graph-neural-network.name: Graph neural network
graph-neural-network.def: A neural network that updates the embedding of each node (here, each protein) with information from its interaction partners.

representation-model.name: Representation model
representation-model.def: A model that converts each input into an embedding; because it is trained without labels (self-supervised), it can draw on very large unannotated corpora.

predictive-model.name: Predictive model
predictive-model.def: A model trained on paired measurements (supervised) to answer one fixed question, so it can predict only what has been measured.

generative-model.name: Generative model
generative-model.def: A model that writes new sequences or states rather than scoring existing ones; its vocabulary determines what it can write.

perturbation-model.name: Perturbation model
perturbation-model.def: A model that, given a cell and an intervention such as a gene knockout, produces the expected expression profile, a state that was never measured. It lies between prediction and generation.

hallucination.name: Hallucination
hallucination.def: A fluent but false statement produced by an LLM.

rag.name: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)
rag.def: Having the model base its answer on retrieved documents, such as papers or database entries, so that answers are current and traceable to a source.

function-calling.name: Function calling
function-calling.def: Letting the model write a request to an external program, such as a database query or an analysis script, and read back the result.

reasoning-model.name: Reasoning model
reasoning-model.def: An LLM trained to write out intermediate steps and rewarded when the final answer to a checkable problem is correct.

mcp.name: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
mcp.def: A standard way, released in late 2024, of connecting tools to models.

skill-files.name: Skill files
skill-files.def: Written instructions an agent loads when needed, such as the steps of a standard analysis or when a tool's output should not be trusted (introduced in 2025).

agent-harness.name: Agent harness
agent-harness.def: The layer that manages long-running agent tasks by repeating the plan–act–revise cycle, providing a workspace for code and files, and asking a human for approval at key decisions.

multi-agent-system.name: Multi-agent system
multi-agent-system.def: A system that assigns roles to separate LLM agents.

tool-route.name: Tool route
tool-route.def: A way an FM enters an agent: the agent reads the FM's output as text. It acts while the agent works.

text-route.name: Text route
text-route.def: A way an FM enters an agent: data are rewritten as language (e.g., each cell as a list of its top genes). It shapes the LLM during training.

encoder-route.name: Encoder route
encoder-route.def: A way an FM enters an agent: embeddings are converted into the LLM's input, so it reads biological data alongside text. It shapes the LLM during training.

verifier-route.name: Verifier route
verifier-route.def: A way an FM enters an agent: an FM scores a reasoning model's answers during training, so its errors become part of the reward. It shapes the LLM during training.

reinforcement-learning.name: Reinforcement learning
reinforcement-learning.def: Training that rewards outcomes. Here it improves how a system uses the knowledge it can reach, but does not move the FM's boundary.

decipherment-questions.name: Decipherment questions
decipherment-questions.def: The questions used to organize the evidence: can any structure be recovered, does it carry meaning, can it be used to write, and which parts remain unreadable? Two more are added in the review: does knowledge extend beyond the training data, and can researchers read it out?

orchestration-boundary.name: Orchestration boundary
orchestration-boundary.def: An agent's own limit in selecting and combining tools; agents with the same tools can differ.

cnn.name: Convolutional neural network (CNN)
cnn.def: A neural network that detects short local patterns, such as a TF binding motif.

simple-baselines.name: Simple baselines
simple-baselines.def: Deliberately simple comparison methods: linear or logistic regression, one-hot encodings of sequence, or simply the average of the training data.

four-layers.name: The four layers of the boundary
four-layers.def: (1) Knowledge missing because observations were never or rarely collected; (2) knowledge hard to learn because the architecture cannot span it or the objective does not reward it (e.g., cause and effect); (3) capability hidden or exaggerated by evaluation; (4) knowledge present in the model but inaccessible to current analysis.

sampling-bias.name: Sampling bias
sampling-bias.def: A model's patterns partly reflecting how often related examples were sampled, rather than the biology itself (for example, unequal sampling across the tree of life).

circular-annotation.name: Circular annotation
circular-annotation.def: A benchmark or annotator scoring well partly because curated databases shaped both the training data and the benchmark labels.

systematic-variation.name: Systematic variation
systematic-variation.def: Expression differences shared across perturbations in general, unrelated to any specific perturbation. They can dominate common metrics, so that predicting an average response scores well.

scaling-laws.name: Scaling laws
scaling-laws.def: In LLMs, the relationship by which performance improves predictably as parameters, training data, and computing budget grow.

stages-of-biological-science.name: Stages of biological science
stages-of-biological-science.def: Observation and classification, then mechanistic understanding of structure, function, and causality, and ultimately engineering: the design of biological systems from first principles.

adaptive-radiation.name: Adaptive radiation
adaptive-radiation.def: After periods of open ecological opportunity that favor large generalists, the adaptive radiation that follows favors smaller organisms fitted to specific niches.

boundary-statement.name: Boundary statement
boundary-statement.def: A structured record of an FM's limits, released with the model, in the spirit of model cards and datasheets and organized by the five design elements.

self-driving-lab.name: Self-driving laboratory
self-driving-lab.def: Robotic platforms that run experiments chosen by a model and return the results for the next round.

shared-literacy.name: Shared literacy
shared-literacy.def: A working understanding of both biology and AI across the two communities. The aim is not to make every biologist a model builder.

model-registry.name: Model registry (proposed)
model-registry.def: A proposed community-maintained resource linking each model to its boundary statement, independent evaluations, known limitations, and replication results.
